lead.p: Honestly? It doesn't matter that much what they teach you. You'll end up learning something else at work anyway. What matters is …

blocks.answer: Honestly? It doesn't matter that much what they teach you. You'll end up learning something else at work anyway. What matters is **being able to adapt**. In my job there's something new to learn every few months, and there's no training for it. Last year it was a whole new customs system. You **read up on** it, you **do your homework** before you talk to clients so you don't **look clueless**, and you basically **teach yourself**. If schools taught kids how to learn, that'd be the most useful thing of all.

lead.p: I'm not sure anyone knows what to teach anymore. I studied translation, and half the agencies I applied to …

blocks.answer: I'm not sure anyone knows what to teach anymore. I studied translation, and half the agencies I applied to **have stopped hiring juniors**. Juniors used to do the simple stuff, like manuals and product descriptions. Now they're **handing** a lot of that work **over to AI**. So **what's the point of** learning skills that could be **out of date by the time you graduate**? **What worries me is** that all that boring, basic work is exactly how people used to learn the job. So who's going to teach us now?

lead.s: Mark, 26, in his first job as an engineer
lead.p: Yes, but practical shouldn't just mean cooking and managing money. When I started this job, it was …

blocks.answer: Yes, but practical shouldn't just mean cooking and managing money. When I started this job, it was **a really steep learning curve**. I had good grades, but nobody had taught me any of the **soft skills**: how to manage my time, ask for help, or cope when things went wrong. You **pick** most of that **up on the job**, usually **the hard way**. It took me months to realise that asking for help isn't a sign of weakness. **I really wish someone had told me** that in school.

cards.ctx: чешский похож на русский — казалось, будет легко
cards.front: <g>For me it was Czech.</g> ~~I thought it's easy to learn a language which is similar.~~
cards.back: For me it was Czech. **It's really close to Russian, but it's a lot harder than you'd think.**
cards.why: harder than you'd think = what anyone expects vs reality. About your own past expectation: I thought it would be easy. ((«сложнее, чем кажется»))

cards.back: Communication with non-technical managers — it's **a lot harder than you'd think**.
cards.why: than I was thinking is a calque. Anyone would think so → than you'd think; only you → than I thought. ((калька с «чем я думала»))

cards.instr: Could be better English: how would you say the grey part?

cards.back: AI helps me make suggestions, but **choosing the best one — that's where I really add value**.

cards.turn: In your work or your life now, where do you really add value?

cards.instr: And this one? No red word this time.
cards.ctx: что остаётся за топ-менеджерами, когда ИИ есть на всех уровнях
cards.front: <g>Networking, department heads, motivation</g> — ~~in this kind of area, I believe AI is still helpless~~.
cards.back: Networking, department heads, motivation — **that's where people still add value**.
cards.why: helpless is usually about people. The box phrase talks about what people do well, not what AI can't do. ((helpless — «беспомощный», обычно о людях))
cards.turn: Two things where people still add value — and AI doesn't, yet.

cards.instr: Could be better English: how would you say the grey part?

cards.front: <g>Top managers still work with paper documents</g> — they could go to jail. ~~That's why we don't use AI for serious work.~~
cards.back: Top managers still work with paper documents — they could go to jail. **That's why we don't hand anything serious over to AI.**

cards.instr: And this one? No red word this time.

p: An international school is changing its curriculum. The head ((AmE: principal)) wants to cut coding and essay writing: “AI can do all that now.” Two new subjects could be added.

blocks.instr: What might they say? Use the box. Then tap the card.

cards.instr: At the school meeting: what might they say? Use the box. Then tap the card.
cards.back: **What's the point of** learning to code? A lot of tech companies have **stopped hiring juniors**. They're **handing all that work over to AI**. Whatever we learn now will be **out of date** by the time we graduate from university.

cards.ctx: **Omar, 52,** a parent. Runs a group of small hotels and does the hiring. Wants to add “how to learn”.
cards.back: I don't need people who know a particular booking system: it'll be **out of date** in two years. They need to **adapt**. I need people who can **read up on** something new and **teach themselves**.

cards.ctx: **Chloe, 24,** a former student. Her first job was in a call centre. Wants to add “dealing with difficult people”.
cards.back: Nobody prepared us for angry customers. I **had to learn the hard way**. And it would have been so easy to teach: two or three role-plays in class.

blocks.instr: In pairs: the dice tells you how many reasons to give, for and against. Use the box. Then decide together.

for: You need to understand code to check what AI writes — **that's where you really add value**.
**It was a steep learning curve**, but it taught me to think step by step.
against: **They're handing it over to AI** — why spend years on it at school?
Lots of tech companies **have stopped hiring juniors**, so why train kids for jobs that may not be there?

for: It's **more important than you'd think** — writing helps you sort out your thoughts.
When AI writes the first draft, I edit it — **that's where I really add value**.
against: **They're handing it over to AI** — nobody writes reports from scratch any more.
We did essay writing every week, and **I've never used it since**.

for: **You never know when it might come in handy** — I never thought I'd live abroad.
Translation apps **only get you so far** — try making friends through one.
against: AI translates everything now — **what's the point of** six years of French?
I did French at school, but when I moved to France, **I had to start from scratch**.

for: It's **more important than you'd think** — people judge you by your spelling.
**You never know when it might come in handy** — when your battery dies, for example.
against: It's **a complete waste of time** — spellcheck does it for us.
**It's out of date.** Nobody writes by hand any more.

for: It's **more useful than you'd think** — in shops, with discounts, when you split a bill.
It was hard, but it paid off — I notice at once when a bill doesn't look right.
against: **What's the point of** mental maths when everyone has a phone?
We spent hours on it, and **I've never used it since**.

for: **They're handing** more and more work **over to AI**, so someone has to check it.
**I learned that the hard way** — kids shouldn't have to.
against: The tools change every month, so what they learn will be **out of date** by the time they leave school.
Kids **pick it up** on their own — and very fast.

for: Everything goes **out of date**, so **you need to adapt** — and that means knowing how to learn.
When I changed careers, **I had to start from scratch**, and nobody had ever shown me how to learn.
against: **I picked it up on the job** — you learn how to learn by doing it, not in a lesson.
**School only gets you so far** — everyone learns differently, so you have to find your own way.

for: AI makes things up, so checking the facts — **that's where you really add value**.
Before I believe a big news story, **I read up on it** — kids should learn to do that too.
against: **What's the point of** a separate subject? Every teacher can do it in their lessons.
You just **do your homework** before you share something — that's a habit, not a subject.

for: My first year as a manager **was a steep learning curve** — nobody had ever taught me how to deal with people.
**I had to learn the hard way**, and I'd love my kids to have it easier.
against: **School only gets you so far** — you learn it from real people, not from role-plays.
It's **more complicated than you'd think** — every difficult person is different, so a school course can't really prepare you.

for: A lot of companies **have stopped hiring juniors**, so young people get fewer chances to learn teamwork at work — school has to do it.
It's **more important than you'd think** — even a team of clever people gets nowhere if they can't work together.
against: They already do group projects all the time — **what's the point of** a whole subject?
**I picked it up on the job** — you can't learn it from a textbook.
